title: Far Side Virtual cover art
lede: James Ferraro’s 2011 cover: an iPad showing a cloud-sky face, pasted over a grainy New York street full of taxis.
summary: Tablet with a sky-collage face over a noisy Manhattan street; spaced multicolour title. 2011.

evidence.note: Inspected the 2000 × 1995 front cover of the Hippos in Tanks digital release in the [Cover Art Archive](https://musicbrainz.org/release/964ec492-5cf2-4635-a54a-0287007f956c/cover-art), in a scratchpad copy. Not stored.

styles.note: A precursor and the start of the “utopian virtual” branch. Partial fit: it quotes then-current tablets and stock imagery rather than 1980s–1990s media, and it has no pastel palette.

context: Wikipedia: Far Side Virtual “drew primarily on ‘the grainy and bombastic beeps’ of then-recent past media, such as Skype, Second Life, Windows XP and the Nintendo Wii,” and the utopian virtual offshoot it began “later became associated with the Frutiger Aero Internet aesthetic.” [Wikipedia: Vaporwave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaporwave). See [Frutiger Aero](style:frutiger-aero).
observed: A black tablet, tilted, fills the left half; its screen shows a face cut out of a blue sky with white clouds, with brush-stroke eyebrows and a red oval mouth.
The background is a Manhattan street with yellow taxis, overlaid with heavy colour noise.
A small copy of the same tablet sits at the upper right; smeared rainbow shapes and a blurred green-and-red blob float at the edges.
The title FARSIDEVIRTUAL runs along the bottom in widely spaced capitals, each letter a different primary colour.
interpretation: It shows the style’s irony toward consumer technology before the palette settled. The widely spaced title already anticipates the fullwidth-letter habit.

rights.statement: Copyrighted album art. No image is stored here.
